title: Appeals to CPF Board for Inclusion in Silver Support Scheme
what_it_is: Appeals to CPF Board for Inclusion in Silver Support Scheme

sections.label: CPF contributions and Silver Support
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Manpower about CPF contributions at age 55 and Silver Support appeal success rates and rejection reasons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) among Singaporeans turning 65 years old in (i) 2016 and (ii) 2017, what proportion would not have had more than $70,000 in total CPF contribution at age 55; and (b) whether the Ministry when formulating the Silver Support Scheme's CPF contribution ceiling has taken into consideration (i) the adjustments made to the CPF contribution rates over the past 20 years; and (ii) the age when the first CPF contribution was made in view of the different CPF contribution rate for different age groups introduced in 1988.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Manpower what is the success rate of appeal for the Silver Support Scheme as at 31 August 2016 and what are the main reasons for the rejection of such appeals.

sections.label: Seniors' CPF contributions
sections.summary: About two-thirds of seniors had total CPF contributions of $70,000 or less when they turned 55, despite contribution rate changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the changes in CPF contribution rates over the years, a majority of our seniors, in fact, about two-thirds of them, have total CPF contributions of $70,000 or less when they turned 55.

sections.label: First Silver Support payouts
sections.summary: One hundred and forty thousand seniors received their first Silver Support payouts in July 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: One hundred and forty thousand of them received their first Silver Support payouts in July 2016.

sections.label: Silver Support explanations and appeals
sections.summary: About 15,000 seniors were explained to, and CPF Board received about 2,300 Silver Support appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So far, they have explained to about 15,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So far, CPF Board has received about 2,300 appeals for Silver Support.

sections.label: Silver Support appeal assessment
sections.summary: Cases not meeting requirements are assessed from a total perspective, with high-income children's cases likely rejected and marginal cases considered case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In short, I think in cases where the senior does not meet the requirements, we will look at the case from the total perspective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If the children are of a higher-income group and if they exceeded the per capita household income criterion by a big margin, those cases are likely to be rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But if they are marginal cases where the number of persons in the household is small, for example, a mother living with a son and the son actually is earning only about, say, $2,500, if this is divided by two persons, the per capita income becomes $1,250 which still exceeds the requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But in those cases, we will look at it from the total perspective and will consider it on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Annual Silver Support eligibility review
sections.summary: Eligibility for Silver Support is reviewed annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The eligibility for Silver Support is reviewed annually.
